name: Senior Care Checklist
description: A comprehensive senior care checklist covering an aging adult's health, safety, daily living, finances, and social needs.

items.text: Keep an up-to-date list of all medications, doses, and schedules
Use a pill organizer and reminders to prevent missed or doubled doses
items.note: Refill prescriptions a few days early to avoid running out.

items.text: Track upcoming doctor, dental, eye, and hearing appointments
Maintain a record of conditions, allergies, and emergency contacts
Stay current on recommended vaccinations and screenings
Confirm health insurance coverage and keep cards accessible
Remove trip hazards like loose rugs, clutter, and cords
Add grab bars in the bathroom and handrails on stairs
Improve lighting in hallways, stairs, and near the bed
Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors regularly
Consider a medical alert device for emergencies
items.note: A wearable alert button lets help be summoned after a fall.

items.text: Make sure exits, locks, and walkways are easy and safe to use
Assess help needed with bathing, dressing, and grooming
Arrange support for housekeeping, laundry, and chores
Plan reliable transportation to appointments and errands
Set up easy ways to stay in touch, like a simple phone or video calls
Review whether in-home help or other care levels are needed
Ensure regular, balanced meals with enough protein and fiber
Keep healthy, easy-to-prepare foods stocked at home
Monitor for unintended weight loss or poor appetite
Encourage enough fluids throughout the day
Follow any dietary restrictions set by the doctor
Consider meal delivery or shared meals to support nutrition and company
Organize bank accounts, bills, and important financial records
Set up automatic payments to avoid missed bills
Confirm a will, power of attorney, and healthcare directive are in place
Store insurance, account, and password information securely
Watch for signs of scams or financial exploitation
Consult a qualified attorney or advisor for major decisions
Schedule regular visits, calls, and family check-ins
Encourage hobbies, faith communities, or senior center activities
Arrange transportation so they can join social events
Watch for signs of loneliness, low mood, or withdrawal
Support physical activity that the doctor has approved
Important: this checklist is general planning information, not medical or legal advice; follow the older adult's doctor and care team, and consult a qualified attorney for legal matters

faq.q: What should a senior care plan include?
faq.a: A good plan covers health and medications, home safety, help with daily living, nutrition, finances and legal documents, and social connection. Reviewing each area regularly helps families adjust care as the older adult's needs change.

faq.q: How do I know when an aging parent needs more help?
faq.a: Watch for missed medications, unpaid bills, weight loss, an unkempt home, missed appointments, falls, or withdrawal from activities. Noting these changes early lets you arrange support before a crisis.

faq.q: What legal documents do seniors need in place?
faq.a: Commonly recommended documents include a will, a durable power of attorney, a healthcare proxy or directive, and access to insurance and account information. Have these prepared with a qualified attorney and stored where trusted family can find them.

faq.q: How can families help seniors stay socially connected?
faq.a: Schedule regular visits and calls, encourage hobbies or community programs, arrange transportation to activities, and consider senior centers or volunteer roles. Social connection supports mood and overall wellbeing.

faq.q: Is this senior care checklist medical or legal advice?
faq.a: No. It is a general planning guide. It is not medical or legal advice — for health decisions follow the older adult's doctor and care team, and consult a qualified attorney for legal and financial matters.
